clue.text: Action of gobbler, bird

definitions.meaning: what a greedy eater does to food, gulping it down
a fork-tailed migrant that skims over fields in summer

explanation.surface: A turkey-like gobbler is described, then a bird is named.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp food down is one sense of the word, and it is also the name of a common forked-tailed summer migrant.

clue.text: Piscatorial beef?

definitions.meaning: relating to fish: here standing for a freshwater fish
beef as a verb means to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: An angler's complaint, or perhaps a fishy cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a freshwater fish and also means to complain or nitpick, slang 'beef'.

clue.text: Two low grades, average lower

parts.note: D and E are two poor exam grades
the second of the two poor grades is E
the mean is the arithmetic average

explanation.surface: A school report showing two poor marks drags down a pupil's average.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade or debase someone is to bring them down in standing.

clue.text: Poet has captured seedy area with craft

indicators.note: the poet word holds the seedy word inside it, as a captor holds a prisoner

parts.note: a bard is a poet
oaty, full of oats, which are seeds of a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A poet has been caught up in some disreputable district full of artisans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' looks like 'shabby' but is taken literally: OATY, full of oat seeds. 'Craft' is boats, not handiwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A dockside area where boats are built, stored and repaired.

clue.text: Watch and look over boy ingesting some LSD

indicators.note: the look-over and boy pieces together swallow the drug dose, which goes inside them
over signals the word for look being turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to look quickly
a son is a boy
a tab is a single dose of LSD

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on a lad who is taking acid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' reads the look word upwards; a tab is a small square of blotting paper soaked in LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor someone closely is to watch them, an idiom of surveillance.

clue.text: Characters furthest apart shrouded in darkness before a dance

indicators.note: the alphabet's end letters are wrapped inside the gloom word as if in a shroud

parts.note: murk is gloom or darkness
A and Z are the letters at opposite ends of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Two figures far apart are lost in the dark before a dance begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Polish folk dance in triple time, also a Chopin piano form.

clue.text: Promise to pin outline on template for garment

indicators.note: pinning holds one thing within another, so the outline letters are held inside the promise word

parts.note: to swear is to promise solemnly

indicators.note: the outline of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dressmaker is told to pin the outline onto a paper pattern for a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover is a type of garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Exhausted female in Irish county …

parts.note: done in means tired out
gal is informal for a girl or woman

explanation.surface: A worn-out woman is found somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in the far north-west of Ireland, known for tweed.

clue.text: Where one might drive later

explanation.surface: A motorist plans to set off along the highway later.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in the future; literally it means farther along the highway.

clue.text: … exhausted, leaving to a standing ovation?

definitions.meaning: worn out and broken down, typically of a machine
read literally, applauded all the way as one exits the stage

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a tired performer exits to rapturous applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang term for worn out and decrepit; the literal reading is being cheered off.

clue.text: Cork in drink flying back

indicators.note: flying back signals the drink word read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a gulp is a swig of drink

explanation.surface: A cork bobs in a drink, then shoots backwards out of the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper that seals a hole, as a cork seals a bottle.

clue.text: Realise needle's threaded then?

definitions.meaning: to grasp or catch on to something
literally, once the yarn has gone onto the needle

explanation.surface: A seamstress grasps something the moment the needle is threaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British phrase for catching on; literally, fibre has gone onto the needle.

clue.text: Get upset about equipment, and call for initial action

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the equipment word
upset means the letters of the word get are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: rig is gear or apparatus
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone gets annoyed with the kit and phones for something to be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles the clue's own word Get to TGE before 'about' wraps it round the equipment; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting something off is the act that starts a process, so it is the first action.

clue.text: Woe is me, head on knees, a state

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grieving person falls to their knees, lamenting the state of things.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest US state, bought from Russia in 1867.

clue.text: Check out and eat powdered food?

definitions.meaning: slang for dying, leaving this life
literally, chewing on fine powdered earth

explanation.surface: A hotel guest settles the bill and eats some dried food.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to die or fail; literally it would mean chewing on dirt.

clue.text: Capering centaurs from old civilisation

indicators.note: capering is leaping about wildly, so the letters dance into a new order

explanation.surface: Mythical horse-men frolic, relics of an ancient culture.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Etruria, the ancient civilisation of central Italy before Rome.

clue.text: Classic very popular, time and time again

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an age is a long period of time, the second time-word

explanation.surface: Something classic stays popular through the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Of enduring high quality, like a fine wine from a good year.

clue.text: Fragrant cap on senior journalist stuffed with cash

indicators.note: stuffed with means the cash word is packed inside the other letters
the cap of a word is its top, its first letter

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a senior journalist
a cent is a coin, a small piece of cash

explanation.surface: A senior editor in a cap is rolling in money and smells sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfumed things have a pleasant aroma.

clue.text: One searing voice?

definitions.meaning: someone who scorches, read as a person who singes
a vocalist, a voice in a choir

explanation.surface: A performer with a scorching voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist performs songs; read cryptically, one who singes or scorches.

clue.text: 7 Across has kiss on record

indicators.note: on places the kiss word after the record word, as if added on to it

parts.note: a roll is an official list or record
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: A sweater, worn while snogging, is caught on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 Across is SWEATER, so the definition is a sweater; 'on' puts the kiss after the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullover with a high turned-over collar is a kind of jumper.

clue.text: Roman army unit member running across island

indicators.note: across means the leg and running words straddle the island letter

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
on means operating or running

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier is jogging across an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of the Roman army of several thousand soldiers.

clue.text: Personality that's awful is recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: rats is an exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: A celebrity whose awful behaviour is remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity or famous figure.

clue.text: Huge breakfast item flipped over, looking to eat it

indicators.note: eating takes one thing inside another, so the egg letters go in the looking word

parts.note: staring is looking hard

indicators.note: flipped over, like an egg cooked over easy, the word is reversed

parts.note: an egg is a breakfast item

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a fried breakfast egg before tucking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped over' suggests a fried egg turned in the pan, which is exactly the reversal; 'it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing or astonishing in scale, enough to make one reel.

clue.text: Injudicious passage from orator, a shambles

indicators.note: passage from means a run of letters is taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A speech from a speaker is a complete mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless, acting without careful thought.

clue.text: The essential part of hugs with an African

indicators.note: the essential part of a word is taken as its middle letters

parts.note: and means with, together

explanation.surface: Warm embraces shared with someone from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the East African country around Lake Victoria.

clue.text: Collection of papers I fed to Rover

indicators.note: fed to means the I is put inside the rover word, like food

parts.note: a dosser is a vagrant, one who roves

explanation.surface: Someone feeds a dog called Rover a bundle of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' looks like a dog's name, but it is a wanderer: DOSSER, British slang for a homeless drifter.
explanation.definitionFit: A file of documents on one subject or person.
